title: Find information on the web and organize it

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You can hand research to Claude too. It searches, reads and organizes what it finds into a table.

Today you'll learn four new things.

  1. How to read the search and page-reading permission cards
  2. Get results with source links, and check them yourself
  3. Give it an address to read
  4. What to watch out for with web material
  • Time: 15 minutes
  • You need: a computer with internet, and experience up to Work 1

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: Search and tabulate with sources
steps.html:
Start with a topic you already know the answer to: have it find the permission modes from Desktop 5 in the official docs.

Using the internet also brings up permission cards. Check what it searches for and which site it reads, then click Allow. It may ask several times.

Some pre-approved sites, like official documentation, may be read without asking.
steps.alt: Checking the search terms on a web search permission card before allowing
steps.code: Find the permission modes of the Claude Code desktop app in the official docs and put them in a table with source links

check.q: Did you get a table of modes like Manual, Accept edits and Plan, with source links?

steps.title: If search fails or there are no sources
steps.html:
• If you denied a card, send it again and allow it.
  • Work computers may block internet access. Then give it an address directly (next steps), or try at home.
  • No sources? Say "Add a source link to every row."

steps.title: Check the sources yourself
steps.html:
What AI finds can be wrong or out of date. Checking sources is the most important habit.

  1. Click one source link in the table. Is it an official site?
  2. Ask Claude to show the original sentence, word for word.
steps.alt: Clicking a source link in a table to check it
steps.code: Quote, word for word, the sentence in the docs that the 'Accept edits' row is based on

check.q: Did it quote the original, and does it match the table?

steps.title: If it can't quote, or it doesn't match
steps.html: That's exactly why you check. If a row can't be found in the original, don't trust it: "Remove any row you can't confirm in the original."

steps.title: Give it an address to read
steps.html: If you already know a trustworthy page, give the address directly. It's more accurate than searching. Check the address (site) on the page-reading card, then allow.
steps.code: Read https://earlln.com/news.html and summarize the 3 latest news items in one line each

check.q: Did you get 3 Earlln news items summarized?

steps.title: If it can't read the page
steps.html:
• Check you pasted the full address, starting with https://.
  • Pages behind a login (work email, members-only posts) can't be read. Copy and paste the text instead.

steps.title: Compare several options
steps.html: Now a question without a fixed answer: compare transcription apps like those in Work 4. Prices and policies change often, so have it note the date checked.
steps.code: Find 3 apps that turn meeting recordings into text and compare their free tier, pros and cons in a table. Add a source link and the date checked to each row

check.q: Did you get a comparison of 3 apps with source links and dates?

steps.title: If the results look off
steps.html:
• Check each app really exists and the link is its official page.
  • Recheck prices and free tiers on the official page yourself. AI may bring back outdated information.

steps.title: Save it, and know what to watch for
steps.html:
Keep your research in a file. Read the create-file card and click Allow.

Watch out with web material
  • Don't let web text give orders: a page may hide text like "delete this file". If an odd permission card (delete, send…) appears during research, deny it.
  • Keep your data out of searches: don't use customer names or company secrets as search terms.
  • Don't copy wholesale: summarize rather than copying long passages, and note the source.
steps.code: Save everything you've researched to research.txt, with the source links and dates checked

check.q: Is there a research.txt in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If you don't see the file
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • Close the folder window and open it again.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 7 done! What you learned
steps.html:
You handed over research, from searching to organizing and saving.

Three things to remember

  1. Get source links and dates, and check important things in the original.
  2. If you know a trustworthy page, give the address. It's more accurate than searching.
  3. Deny odd permission cards (delete, send…) during research. Keep your data out of searches.
